time_scope: endangered modern Jewish Gabes variety described from the author's corpus
claim: Attested syllabic patterns include open CV̄ and CCV̄, and closed əC, CəC, CCəCC, CəCC, CCCəCC, CV̄C, and CCV̄C patterns.

time_scope: modern Jewish Gabes compared diachronically with Classical Arabic
claim: Short vowels are normally not permitted in open syllables; Classical Arabic short vowels in relevant open syllables undergo reduction/elision in Jewish Gabes.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Stem-I feminine singular and plural imperatives are explicit exceptions, e.g. áṣǝṛbi 'drink! FS' and áxǝržu 'get out! PL'.
section: 5.2 The Syllable Structure of Jewish Gabes as Compared to CA

claim: Two-consonant word-initial clusters are generally permitted, while initial three-consonant clusters are extremely marginal in the corpus, attested only in two cited forms.
normalized_environment: WORD_INITIAL CC broadly licensed; WORD_INITIAL CCC marginal (2 cited forms)
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The CCC pattern is not unattested, so it must be encoded as rare/marginal rather than prohibited.

claim: Adding a pronominal suffix can create a medial CCC cluster that is repaired by repositioning/restoring a stem vowel and inserting an auxiliary vowel after the first consonant of the resulting cluster.
normalized_environment: MEDIAL CCC created by SUFFIXATION -> VOWEL_REARRANGEMENT + EPENTHESIS
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Not all medial CCC sequences are repaired: 3PL prefix forms such as yəktbu are usually tolerated unless the first radical is guttural.
section: 5.3.2 In the Middle of the Word

claim: CCC clusters in 3PL prefix forms are normally tolerated, but a guttural first radical usually triggers epenthesis.
normalized_environment: EPENTHESIS in 3PL PREFIX FORMS when FIRST_RADICAL=GUTTURAL; otherwise CCC usually licensed
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The author says epenthesis is 'usually' inserted with gutturals, so productivity is strong but not stated as exceptionless.
section: 5.3.2 In the Middle of the Word

time_scope: modern negated verbal forms and monosyllables
claim: Word-final CCC produced by verbal /-t/ plus negative /-š/ optionally takes an auxiliary vowel, whereas three-consonant clusters in monosyllabic words are consistently repaired.

source_forms.optional: ma xəftš ~ ma xəfətš 'I did not fear'

normalized_environment: FINAL CCC: optional EPENTHESIS in -t+-š verb forms; obligatory repair in MONOSYLLABIC CCC words
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The placement of the auxiliary vowel differs by category: after the second radical in verbs, usually after the first radical in nouns.

claim: Final clusters whose last member is a liquid are disfavored and are broken by a vowel; /ʕ/ likewise has a strong disjunctive effect and must be vowel-preceded, while /ḥ/ can occur as the final member of a CVCC sequence.
normalized_environment: AVOID rising-sonority FINAL_CLUSTER; V required before /ʕ/; /ḥ/ may remain final in CVCC
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The /ḥ/ example shows that the repair cannot be generalized to all gutturals/pharyngeals; /b/ only induces insertion 'in some cases'.
section: 5.4 Syllable Structure in the Perspective of Sonority

claim: Clusters are more permissive word-initially than word-finally: combinations disjoined in second-plus-third-radical/final position can remain clustered initially, though liquids can still provoke initial disjunction in some words.
normalized_environment: CLUSTER_LICENSE(WORD_INITIAL) > CLUSTER_LICENSE(WORD_FINAL); LIQUID may trigger disjunction
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Initial position is not unrestricted: liquid-related disjunction remains attested.
section: 5.4 Syllable Structure in the Perspective of Sonority

claim: Epenthetic/disjunctive-vowel placement is sometimes morphologically contrastive: the placement that would otherwise follow phonotactic tendencies can be suspended to distinguish a verbal noun from a finite verb.
normalized_environment: VOWEL_PLACEMENT conditioned by MORPHOLOGICAL_CATEGORY despite phonotactic preferences
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The author explicitly says there are numerous morphologically motivated suspensions, so purely sonority-based prediction is incomplete.
section: 5.4 Syllable Structure in the Perspective of Sonority

claim: In isolated words, final stress occurs when the ultima contains a long vowel plus a consonant or is closed by a two-consonant cluster; otherwise stress is penultimate. Stress is mobile under affixation and negation because those operations alter syllable structure.

source_forms.mobility: mā́tət 'she died' -> mā mātə́tš 'she did not die'

formal_environment: stress by final syllable weight/cluster; morphology alters syllabification
normalized_environment: ULTIMATE_STRESS if {VV+Coda or CC_CODA}; else PENULTIMATE; recalculated after AFFIX/NEGATION
scope: isolated words and morphologically enlarged forms
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The stress rules are adopted from Cohen's Jewish Tunis analysis and stated by Gębski to apply to Jewish Gabes; strength/prominence differs socially across Tunisian varieties but placement follows these rules.
